title: The Day Water Changed Its Mind

pages.text: The Day Water Changed Its Mind A story about matter and its states

Ms. Gomez explained that matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas. Ice is a solid because it keeps its shape. Water is a liquid because it flows and fits its container. Steam is a gas because it spreads out into the air. “Today,” said Ms. Gomez, “we will watch water change from one state to another.”

Slowly, the edges of the ice cubes turned shiny. Tiny drops of water slid down the sides. “This change is called melting,” said Ms. Gomez. “Melting happens when a solid gains heat energy and becomes a liquid.” The melting point of water is 0°C, or 32°F. While the ice is melting, the temperature stays constant until all the ice has changed into liquid water.

Next, the class watched the pot on the hot plate. Tiny bubbles formed at the bottom. Soon they rushed to the surface, and steam drifted into the air. ‘This is boiling,’ Ms. Gomez explained. ‘Boiling happens when a liquid changes into a gas.’ The boiling point of water is 100°C, or 212°F, at sea level. During boiling, the temperature also stays constant until the water finishes changing into gas.

Then Ms. Gomez showed the class a cup that had been left in the freezer box. Yesterday it had been liquid water. Now it was solid ice. ‘That change is called freezing,’ said Riya. ‘Exactly,’ said Ms. Gomez. ‘Freezing happens when a liquid loses heat energy and becomes a solid.’ The freezing point of water is 0°C, or 32°F, and during freezing the temperature stays constant until the change is complete.

At the end of class, Riya and Ethan wrote down the big idea: Melting changes a solid to a liquid. Freezing changes a liquid to a solid. Boiling changes a liquid to a gas. Water melts and freezes at 0°C (32°F), and it boils at 100°C (212°F). Most important of all, during a phase change, the temperature remains constant until the change is complete. Science Element: Matter can change state when it gains or loses energy.
